clue.text: Witches meeting to hear case of silent city

parts.note: a gathering of witches is a coven
a judge who hears a case tries it, so to hear a case is to try

explanation.surface: Witches gather to hear the case of a city that has fallen silent.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them, which is why the city is called silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The English idiom of sending a person to this Midlands city means shunning them in silence, hence a city of silence.

clue.text: Pampered, if half-boiled

explanation.surface: A spoilt child, or a softly cooked egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is to over-indulge someone, and also to cook an egg gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Beer vital to new arrangement if genuine

indicators.note: new arrangement says the letters of Beer and vital are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Beer is vital to any new arrangement worth the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Veritable means real or true, used to stress that something deserves its description.

clue.text: Such being the heart of the matter

definitions.text: Such being the heart of the matter

parts.words: Such being the heart of the matter
parts.note: the core of an atom, the stuff matter is made of, so the phrase describes what relates to that core

explanation.surface: This is what lies at the centre of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heart of the matter' sounds like the crux of an argument; here matter is physical matter and its heart the atomic nucleus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear means relating to the nucleus, the central core of each atom of matter.

clue.text: Disastrous effect of Cromwell on Marie

definitions.text: Disastrous effect of Cromwell on Marie

parts.words: Disastrous effect of Cromwell on Marie
parts.note: the music-hall song in which the singer is one of the wrecks that Cromwell knocked about a bit

explanation.surface: Oliver Cromwell brought calamity upon a woman called Marie.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd, a British music-hall star, sang 'One of the Ruins that Cromwell Knocked About a Bit'; Cromwell's effect on her made her a ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin, disastrous, which is what Cromwell was to the castle wrecks of the song.

clue.text: Nasty vapour on motorway as Mother follows

indicators.note: follows places the word for Mother after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, read here as the letters M and I
taken as written
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A foul haze hangs over the motorway as Mother drives behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unhealthy or foul-smelling vapour, the bad air once blamed for disease.

clue.text: Unfair prosecutions of spinsters?

parts.note: court cases declared invalid, read also as the ordeals of unmarried women, each a Miss on trial

explanation.surface: Unjust court cases brought against single women.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MISS TRIALS, the word becomes trials of misses, unmarried women.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial made void by a fundamental error, an unfair prosecution.

clue.text: Where I too appear in Latin inscriptions

definitions.text: Where I too appear in Latin inscriptions

parts.words: Where I too appear in Latin inscriptions
parts.note: the Latin tomb motto meaning 'even I am in this pastoral paradise', spoken by Death

explanation.surface: A place named in Latin carvings where I also appear.
explanation.walkthrough: The motto 'Et in Arcadia ego' ('I too am in Arcadia') is inscribed on tombs in classical paintings by Poussin and Guercino.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised rural paradise of Greek pastoral poetry, named in the famous Latin tomb motto.

clue.text: Sirenian man in driving position

parts.note: a sea mammal of the dugong order, pictured as a man waiting at the golf tee to drive off

explanation.surface: A man stands ready at the tee to drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: Sirenian is the definition; the rest pictures MAN AT TEE, which run together with one T sound like the animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirenians are the order of aquatic mammals that includes dugongs and sea cows, so one is a sea cow of that order.

clue.text: General orders drive, cites muddle

indicators.note: muddle tells us the letters of drive and cites are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive are given while the officer muddles his citations.
explanation.definitionFit: Directives are instructions issued by an authority, orders of a general kind.

clue.text: Is incapable of hypocrisy

explanation.surface: Someone simply cannot manage to be hypocritical.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as the contraction it means 'is unable'; as a noun it means insincere, pious talk.

clue.text: Renowned landlord's financial authority?

parts.note: a famous landlord is one who lets property and is held in credit, while the whole phrase is also a banker's document authorising payment

explanation.surface: A famous landlord holds sway over money matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter' is one who lets, so a renowned landlord is a letter of credit (credit as good name); the real phrase is a bank's guarantee of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: This bank document authorises a holder to draw funds, a written financial guarantee.

clue.text: Comes ashore and strips the tree

explanation.surface: A sailor lands and then peels the bark off a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To debark is to disembark from a ship, and also to remove bark from timber.

clue.text: They remind us of Jap liquor found in donjons

indicators.note: found in puts the liquor inside the word for donjons

parts.note: a donjon is the great tower of a castle, its keep
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Bottles of Japanese rice wine discovered in castle towers bring back memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepsakes are mementos, objects kept to recall a person or occasion.

clue.text: Father holds a high honour for this remedy

indicators.note: holds means the word for Father is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father
in card games the ace is the highest honour card, so a high honour is an ace

explanation.surface: Dad is awarded a great distinction for this cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a cure-all, a remedy supposed to fix every ill.

clue.text: Study different ratios of business combines

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of ratios in another order

explanation.surface: Analyse various proportions found in company groupings.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are associations of companies joined for a common venture, the plural of consortium.

clue.text: King John of legend

parts.note: the medieval legend of a Christian priest-king in the East, whose title stood before the name John

explanation.surface: A legendary monarch named John.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the English King John: Prester John was a mythical Christian king said to rule in Asia or Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Prester, meaning priest, was the title of the mythical eastern monarch John of medieval legend.

clue.text: Discounts are best, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in no particular order, so the letters of are and best are scrambled

explanation.surface: Price cuts are the best deal whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebates are partial refunds or reductions in the amount to pay.

clue.text: In USA, maybe, brothers appear in secret

indicators.note: In tells us the brothers are placed inside the rearranged letters
maybe suggests USA is one possible order of its letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of USA as written

explanation.surface: In America, perhaps, some brothers turn up in a hush-hush manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In USA' reads as a location in America, but 'In' is the container signal and 'maybe' marks USA as fodder to be rearranged around the brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa is Latin for 'under the rose', an old emblem of confidentiality, meaning privately.

clue.text: Agrees to have sent in a stupid chap

indicators.note: in tells us the word sent is placed inside the word for a stupid chap

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to let a foolish man be dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or give consent.

clue.text: Signs on at international matches

parts.note: taken as written
Test matches are international cricket or rugby fixtures

explanation.surface: A player signs up for international fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness formally, as one does by signing a document.

clue.text: " Ambition should be made of — stuff " (J Caesar)

definitions.text: " Ambition should be made of — stuff " (J Caesar)

parts.words: " Ambition should be made of — stuff " (J Caesar)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Mark Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony says Caesar wept for the poor, and 'Ambition should be made of sterner stuff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing comparative means harsher or more severe, the word that completes Antony's line.

clue.text: Not the main training tracks

parts.note: railway lines off the main line, with training read as of trains rather than of practice

explanation.surface: Secondary courses used for practice runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training tracks' suggests athletics; read 'train-ing tracks', it means rails for trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidings are short railway tracks beside the main line where trains are parked or shunted.

clue.text: Tale of two tots — but not from the bottle

definitions.text: Tale of two tots — but not from the bottle

parts.words: Tale of two tots — but not from the bottle
parts.note: the old story of two small children lost in a forest, with tots also read as drinks drawn from the cask rather than bottled

explanation.surface: A story about two little children, with a hint they are not bottle-fed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tots are small children and also small drinks; beer 'in the wood' is served from the barrel, not the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional English tale tells of two abandoned children who die in a forest, and beer from a cask is said to be drawn from the wood.

clue.text: Bismarck loves to take in a race

indicators.note: take in means the letters for loves enclose the race

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O, so loves give two Os
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: The German chancellor enjoys going to watch a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the nineteenth-century Prussian statesman, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Site of the gardens of Pan

definitions.text: Site of the gardens of Pan

parts.words: Site of the gardens of Pan
parts.note: the London park where J M Barrie's boy who never grew up has his statue and first adventures

explanation.surface: Where the god Pan keeps his gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is not the Greek god but Peter Pan, whose statue stands in a royal park in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's statue stands in the London park named after this borough, the setting of Barrie's first Pan story.

clue.text: Large automobiles given to top actors

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, meaning large
cars are automobiles

explanation.surface: Big limousines are handed to the leading film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood's Academy Awards are statuettes awarded to the best performers, so they are what top actors are given.

clue.text: Restates afresh extracts from legal records.

indicators.note: afresh asks for the letters of the word Restates to be set out anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A clerk once more repeats passages taken from court files.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an estreat is a true copy or extract of a court record, such as a fine to be collected.
